headline: Learned embeddings transfer across protein, mRNA, promoter and genomic sequence tasks
label: Learned Biological Sequence Representations
summary: Pretrained protein language model embeddings are being repurposed across modalities and tasks, including mRNA and bacterial promoter sequences.
synthesis: The dominant thread is reuse of learned sequence representations, either pretrained or trained contrastively, transferred to new prediction targets. TREAD applies protein language model embeddings to residue-level repeat annotation and reports matching or beating HMMER. ProtmRNA adapts ESM-2 to mRNA sequences via cross-modal transfer, matching mRNA language models with less than half the pre-training. C3P contrastively aligns bacterial promoters with protein language model embeddings, reporting multi-fold gains over gLMs. Other items pursue distinct routes: MiAE, a masked SE(3)-invariant autoencoder for protein structure, a CNN autoencoder feeding a random forest for protein-protein interaction, and RoBERTa classification of serialized gene pairs for operon prediction. DiscrimAlign and SpliceRead are less representation-centric. The novelty lies mainly in cross-modal transfer and text-serialized genomic input rather than in any single architecture.
